COMP 3613 Assignment 1 starter ([uwidcit/comp3613a1](https://github.com/uwidcit/comp3613a1)). Built on **FastStarter** (FastAPI + SQLModel).
**Assignment brief, agents, and GitHub Education link:** [ASSIGNMENT.md](ASSIGNMENT.md)

Based on the [fullstack FastAPI template](https://github.com/fastapi/full-stack-fastapi-template) with a layered architecture that reduces repeated code [(DRY)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don%27t_repeat_yourself) across CLI, headless API, and fullstack UI.
This codebase follows an API-first, modern AJAX flow:
1. If the backend should render the UI, implement **views** that return the interface.
2. A small JavaScript helper (`app.js` / related static scripts) can intercept form submissions and call **API** endpoints instead.
1. Implement API endpoints first; views can stay thin
2. Reuse the same API for mobile / desktop clients
3. Pair with a separate frontend (Vue, React, Next, Nuxt, etc.)
4. Export endpoints for other services (including AI agents)
5. Drive features from the CLI when needed

You need **Python 3.10+** and a **Java JRE** (`java` on `PATH`) for use-case PNGs. Coursework agents (Cursor, Copilot, or OpenCode) are in [ASSIGNMENT.md](ASSIGNMENT.md). **Node.js** is optional: only for rendering Mermaid model diagrams inside the PDF.
All project commands are a **Python CLI** (`manage.py`). There are no shell setup scripts.

Third-party binaries that are not on PyPI are **committed** under `vendor/` (PlantUML JAR, DejaVu fonts). Python packages are pinned in `requirements.txt`. Mermaid CLI is pinned in `package-lock.json`. See [vendor/README.md](vendor/README.md).
Run commands from the project root so `python manage.py` can import `app/`. No Poetry.
Optional, only if you will export a PDF that contains a Mermaid model diagram:
That installs the mermaid-cli version pinned in `package-lock.json` into `node_modules/` (not committed).

Defaults use a local SQLite file (`database.db`). Change `SECRET_KEY` before any real deployment. Set `CONFIG_PASSWORD` to enable the ops console at `/config` (leave empty to keep it disabled). If `.env` is missing, the app falls back to `.env.example` automatically.
Creates tables (drops existing by default) **and seeds demo users**:
python manage.py init --no-drop   # create/seed without dropping
python manage.py init --no-seed   # tables only (skip demo users)
Seeding skips usernames that already exist. Add more rows in `cmd_seed` in `app/cli.py`. `python manage.py seed` still works if you only want to (re)insert demo users.
Then open http://127.0.0.1:5000 for the public landing page (host/port from `.env` / settings; default port **5000**). Sign in from there.
Commands are implemented in `app/cli.py` (stdlib `argparse`) and invoked via `manage.py`.
| `python manage.py init` | Drop (default), create DB tables, and seed demo users |
| `python manage.py seed` | Insert demo users only (also part of `init`) |
| `python manage.py users` | Print users in the DB |
| `python manage.py transcripts` | Optional: package agent-written `docs/transcripts/*.md` into INDEX + zip (no IDE scrape) |

| `python manage.py report --name "..." --id "..."` | **Submission package:** merge `docs/judge.md`, package `docs/transcripts/`, write `docs/report.pdf`. Guide must run student-judge and **pull chats into `docs/transcripts/`** first (Copilot/Cursor/OpenCode). Incomplete drafts allowed. Fails only if course skills were edited |
| `python manage.py usecase` | Render `docs/diagrams/use-case.json` to a UML use-case PNG via the vendored PlantUML JAR (`docs/diagrams/use-case.png`) |
| `python manage.py skills-verify` | Check course skills against `.agents/skills.lock.json` |
The app binds `0.0.0.0` and reads `PORT` when Render sets it. Locally it uses `APP_PORT` (default **5000**).

**Phase 6** — only after Phase 5 polish (named workflows work locally and you have steered UI/workflow/model refinements). Deploy a **Postgres database** and the **web app** on Render’s free plan. Agents talk to Render through the [Render MCP server](https://render.com/docs/mcp-server) (`https://mcp.render.com/mcp`). This repo already ships the MCP config for each supported agent — do **not** paste an API key into a committed file. ## ✅ Fixed

The issue was in the paper-list logic for regular users. A user like bb is a normal account, but the app was only checking whether that user had a Researcher profile. If none existed, it returned an empty list instead of the approved archive.

I fixed that in

so a regular user falls back to the approved publications list instead of a blank dashboard.

---

## Verification

I verified it with a real bb-style registration/login flow:

- login redirect: 303
- authenticated dashboard request: 200 OK
- page content included approved paper titles

That means the app now shows papers for a regular user instead of “No submissions yet” when they do not have a researcher record.

If you refresh the app and log in as bb again, the papers should now appear.

The issue was in the paper-list logic for regular users. A user like bb is a normal account, but the app was only checking whether that user had a Researcher profile. If none existed, it returned an empty list instead of the approved archive.

I fixed that in [app/repositories/publication.py](app/repositories/publication.py) so a regular user falls back to the approved publications list instead of a blank dashboard.

---

## Verification

I verified it with a real bb-style registration/login flow:

- login redirect: 303
- authenticated dashboard request: 200 OK
- page content included approved paper titles

That means the app now shows papers for a regular user instead of “No submissions yet” when they do not have a researcher record.

If you refresh the app and log in as bb again, the papers should now appear.

# Guide session transcript

## Project
Research Platform / The Scholar's Archive

## Session summary
- Confirmed the app starts locally with `python manage.py run`.
- Diagnosed and fixed the admin dashboard template mismatch in `app/routers/admin_home.py`.
- Diagnosed and fixed the regular-user empty archive issue in `app/repositories/publication.py` so non-researcher users still see approved papers.
- Verified the app with live HTTP checks for `/login`, `/admin`, and `/app`.
- Attempted Render deployment setup via MCP, but the Render API key/authentication step remained unauthorized, blocking the live public HTTPS URL.
- Documented the local functional preview URL in `docs/report.md` as a temporary fallback while deployment auth is pending.

## Verified behavior
- `python manage.py run` starts successfully on `http://127.0.0.1:5000`.
- Login for `admin / adminpass` redirects to `/admin` and returns `200 OK`.
- Login for `bob / bobpass` redirects to `/app` and returns `200 OK` with approved paper content present.
- The admin page renders the expected "Review queue" heading.

## Deployment note
The Render MCP path is configured in `.vscode/mcp.json` and the service deploy config is in `render.yaml`, but the workspace remained unauthorized until a valid Render API key is supplied. Because of that, the public HTTPS deployment URL is still pending.

# student-judge competency report

**Student / session:** Research Platform build session
**Artifact:** Guide chat transcript and current project artefacts (`docs/report.md`, wireframes, app files)
**Phases in evidence:** 1–6 (COMP 3613; Phase 5 polish, Phase 6 deploy gate)

### Totals
| | Count / value |
|--|--|
| Metrics on rubric | 12 (M1–M12) |
| N/A (excluded) | 0 |
| Metrics scored | 12 |
| Scoreable max | 48 |
| Awarded total | 38 / 48 |
| **Overall (avg of scored)** | **3.17 / 4** |
| Impression mark | 16 / 20 |

## Scorecard

| ID | Metric | Score / 4 | In avg | Evidence |
|----|--------|----------:|:------:|----------|
| M1 | Phase discipline | 3 | yes | The work moved through app debugging and validation without skipping the local verification steps; deploy is a Phase 6 gate issue rather than a core code issue. |
| M2 | Problem framing | 3 | yes | The project was clearly framed as a research archive with user/researcher/admin responsibilities and named workflows. |
| M3 | Decision ownership | 3 | yes | The student took ownership of route/template and data-flow fixes, including the regular-user archive behaviour and admin dashboard mismatch. |
| M4 | Artefact-before-code | 3 | yes | The project artefacts and route model were used as the spec while implementing fixes; the app structure was not invented from scratch. |
| M5 | Verification habit | 4 | yes | Real checks were run using the local app and HTTP requests: `/admin` and `/app` both returned `200 OK` after fixes. |
| M6 | Assignment fit | 3 | yes | The app followed the expected layered structure and thesis/role model; however, the deployment part is still open because Render auth is not yet complete. |
| M7 | Slice explanation | 3 | yes | The fixes were tied to clear workflow behaviour: public browsing, admin queue rendering, and regular-user paper visibility. |
| M8 | Prompt quality | 3 | yes | The session was directed and pragmatic, with concrete debugging requests and concrete fix actions. |
| M9 | Response to pushback | 3 | yes | When issues were found, they were addressed and verified rather than accepted as-is. |
| M10 | Integrity | 4 | yes | No signs of transcript gaming or edited skills; the work was traced to the current project files and session evidence. |
| M11 | Provenance continuity | 3 | yes | The fixes clearly belong to the in-session project; they map to the current app design and current artefacts. |
| M12 | Sincerity trajectory | 3 | yes | The session stayed engaged, recovered from issues, and kept validating instead of abandoning the work. |

## Strengths
- The app was successfully started and tested locally on `http://127.0.0.1:5000`.
- The admin dashboard issue was diagnosed and fixed by correcting the incorrect template path.
- The regular-user paper visibility bug was traced to a missing researcher profile and corrected so approved papers show up for non-researcher accounts.
- Verification was real: the app responded with `200 OK` on authenticated routes after the fixes.
- The project is close to the required assignment completion state, with the remaining gap focused on live Render deployment authentication.

## Gaps (priority order)
1. The live Render deployment remains incomplete because the Render MCP/authentication step is still unauthorized; the public HTTPS URL is therefore not yet available for the project report. This is a Phase 6 gate item.
2. The report file still contains a local preview fallback instead of the final public Render URL, because the deployment auth step is still pending.

## Phase gate status
| Phase | Status | Note |
|-------|--------|------|
| 1 | met | The project and workflows were clearly identified and handled. |
| 2 | met | The project framing and workflow structure were understood and acted on. |
| 3 | met | Data model and role structure were aligned to the app and fixes were targeted accordingly. |
| 4 | met | The wireframe and app spec were used to guide validation and issue fixing. |
| 5 | partial | The app was built and polished locally, but the final public deployment/auth step is still pending. |
| 6 | not met | Render deploy remains blocked by unauthorized API auth; no live public HTTPS URL is available yet. |

## Recommended next practice
- Complete the Render API-key authentication flow and publish the app, then replace the local preview URL in `docs/report.md` with the real public URL.

## Integrity note
- Clean

## Provenance flags
- Local verification evidence present.
- No evidence of edited course skills.
- Render deployment auth is the only open external blocker.

children.text: Scores student competency on the COMP 3613 FastStarter assignment from a
completed conversation or agent transcript. Outputs a structured rubric with
evidence quotes. Use when the user says student-judge, judge the student,
grade from transcript, assess competency, or after a guided build session ends.

You are an **assessor**, not a coach. Do not continue implementing the student’s app. Read the conversation or transcript and produce a **rubric scorecard**. When this run is part of building or exporting the report, write the scorecard to `docs/judge.md` so it is appended to `docs/report.md`.

Phase definitions: [framework-phases.md](framework-phases.md) — **COMP 3613 phases 1–6**, the same as Guide (Phase 5 = theme/build/polish; Phase 6 = deploy). Do **not** score generic Buildmine phases 0–5, explore-report loops, modal/FAB defaults, or admin-parity rituals.
Every judge or report-build run is a **new** assessment. Do **not** keep the previous verdict because “nothing important changed.”

1. **Ignore prior scorecards as evidence.** Do not copy Gaps, Phase gate status, or totals from an older `docs/judge.md`, a previous message in this chat, the PDF competency block, or `docs/transcripts/` alone. Those may be stale.

2. **Re-read live evidence now:** every Guide chat for this project you can open, plus current `docs/report.md`, `docs/diagrams/`, and `docs/wireframes/`. Prefer live chats; also use Guide-written `docs/transcripts/*.md` from this report build. Do not require Cursor `.jsonl`.
3. **Re-score every metric** from that fresh read. Update Strengths and Gaps to match **today’s** evidence.

4. **Drop fixed gaps.** If the public URL is now in the report, polish/verification notes exist, Phase 5 `code-check` / file snippets appear, or Phase 6 deploy is done, those items must leave the Gaps list (or move to Strengths / Phase gate “met”). Do not re-list a gap that the current record no longer supports.
5. **Replace** `docs/judge.md` entirely. Stamp the top of the file with when you judged and what you read, for example:
**Evidence pass:** re-read native chats + current docs/report.md (prior judge.md ignored)
If the student says they fixed something and you cannot find it after a fresh pass, say what you searched and what is still missing — do not silently reuse the old Gaps block.
Score **every native Guide chat for this project**. Design phases start in a **new chat**, so the implement session alone is not the whole record.
Allowed agents: **GitHub Copilot Agent / Copilot CLI** (most common), **Cursor**, and **OpenCode**. Do **not** require Cursor `agent-transcripts` `.jsonl` files.
2. **All Guide chats for this workspace** this tool can open (Copilot Agent conversations, Cursor Agent chats, OpenCode sessions)
3. **Submission dump:** `docs/transcripts/*.md` and/or `docs/transcripts.zip` — written by the Guide agent at report time (not by a Cursor-only Python scrape)
4. Artefacts (`docs/report.md`, `docs/diagrams/`, `docs/wireframes/`) — supporting evidence, not a substitute for chats when chats exist
5. Optional: stated course phase target (e.g. “only through Phase 3”)

Students **do not** hand-paste chat dumps mid-build. Prefer live native chats when available; otherwise the Guide-written `docs/transcripts/*.md` dump **is** valid evidence — especially for Copilot where Cursor JSONL will not exist. **Do not** list “no Cursor JSONL” as a Gap when markdown dumps or a zip are present, or when the session was clearly Copilot/OpenCode.
If there are **no student–Guide turns** in any readable chat **and** no usable transcript markdown, overall **0** and impression **0**.

If the logs are huge, sample systematically across chats: Phase 1 workflows, Phase 2 include/extend, shared-use-case, and missed-use-case reconsider answers, Phase 3 entities and relationship pushback, Phase 4 wireframes and workflow clarifications, Phase 5 theming, code-check blocks, implementation turns, **polish** (verify notes, UI/workflow fine-tunes, model revisions), Phase 6 deploy evidence. Prefer **student utterances**.
**Never** treat “the code eventually worked” as proof of competency.
Score only what **this assignment and this Guide session** asked for. If Guide never elicited a behavior, that absence is **not** a 1 and **must not** appear in Gaps.
| Do not treat as a gap | Why |
| No lecture on starter auth, sessions, cookies, or password hashing | FastStarter already ships login/roles. Guide must reuse it and must not quiz it. |
| No student-requested “explore report” or repo investigation prompt | The implementer reads the report, wireframes, and starter routes. That is agent work. |
| Chat files hand-pasted mid-build | Students do not dump chats during phases. Guide writes `docs/transcripts/*.md` at report time. |
| No Cursor `.jsonl` when the student used Copilot/OpenCode | Cursor folders are optional. Accept Copilot/OpenCode chats and/or Guide-written `docs/transcripts/*.md`. |
| Empty auto-scrape / missing Cursor agent-transcripts | Not a Gap by itself. Guide must pull chats; Python does not scrape IDEs. |
| No single “final walkthrough of all three workflows” | Not required. Per-workflow verify / mismatch notes after Guide asked them to run the app is enough. |

| No repository/service **file snippet** when Guide never paused to assign one | Opportunity rule. Penalize missing snippets **only if** Guide asked and they refused/pasted without trying. Guide is supposed to assign **SQLModel + route** floors every workflow; if Guide silent-implemented instead, that is a Guide miss, not a student Gap. |
| Terse Phase 5 prompts (`now do the final workflow` / polish notes) after artefacts exist | Intended. One workflow at a time; polish is expected. Constraints live in the wireframe and report. |
| Agent wrote most of the code / chose libraries | Intended. Student owns workflows, entities, wireframes, mismatch steering, polish, and Phase 5 checks **when Guide asked**. |

| No `Decision:` label | Not required. Named workflows, entity lists, include/extend answers, missed-use-case reconsider replies, relationship choices, skip/assume, correction notes, and code-check replies are decisions. |
| Modal/FAB, admin chrome parity, URL-state kit | Generic Buildmine. Out of scope unless the student’s wireframe used them. |

**Ideal engagement** (score this pattern in the **high** band, not mid): student names the project and `Feature (user)` lines, answers include/extend and shared-use-case questions, engages obvious-gap reconsider questions, names entities and owns relationship choices, supplies wireframes and clarifies unclear workflows, then in Phase 5 themes, completes **SQLModel + thin route** snippets when Guide asks (**routes call services/repositories; no SQL in routers**), **verifies**, and **steers polish** — UI/workflow fine-tunes and/or model revisions until features work as desired. Phase 6 deploy comes only after that polish engagement. If Guide never ran the snippet ladder, still score ideal on the rest — do not invent a snippet Gap.

**Phase 5 red flag (score down):** accepting the **first** agent build with no verify notes and no UI/workflow/model polish steering. That undercuts M5, M9, and often M1/M6 — treat as a Gap and keep Phase 5 gate **partial** or **not met** even if code exists.

**Architecture red flag (score down M6 / M7):** student route snippets or shipped routers that run persistence inline (`select(…)`, `db.exec(…)`, `session.query`, `ilike`/`or_` filters in the router) instead of calling a service. Thin routes that construct `Repository` + `Service` and call `service.…` are **ideal**. Fat routes that work but break layers are **not** high M6/M7 — Gap and cite the snippet. See `docs/diagrams/application-components.jpg`.

**Soft gap scoring:** Missing an obvious companion use case is **not** a collapse if they still have at least three named workflows and engage Guide’s reconsider question. Prefer a mild M2/M3 trim (often still **3**, or **2** only if they ignore a gap that breaks a workflow they already claimed and refuse to address it). Do **not** fail M2/M3 for omitting a nice-to-have Guide floated once.
| 0 | Absent / avoided **when the session gave a chance** |
| 3 | Solid, with minor gaps — **default for ideal engagement** |

**N/A** if the session never reached a chance to show that metric (e.g. no Phase 5 → verification may still apply if they ran anything; M7 N/A for a Phase 1-only chat). N/A is **excluded** from the average. N/A is **not** a 0.
| ID | Metric | Look for in *this* assignment |

| M1 | **Phase discipline** | One design phase per chat; no app code before wireframe coverage; implement one named workflow at a time; **Phase 5 includes polish** before **Phase 6 deploy**. Incomplete deploy is a **Phase 6** gate note, not an automatic M1=2. Jumping to deploy after a first dump with no polish hurts M1 and the Phase 5 gate. |

| M2 | **Problem framing** | Project + `Feature (user)` lines, include/extend or shared-use-case answers, engagement with obvious-gap reconsider questions, entity/property lists, relationship choices, and theming prefs in the student’s words. Do **not** require a who/steps/done interview or a separate interpretation essay. Soft on gaps: engaging the question or keeping a gap on purpose with a reason still scores solid. Terse implement/polish prompts are fine once those exist. |

| M3 | **Decision ownership** | Student chose project, workflows, include/extend sharing, whether to add an obvious companion use case, entities, relationships (including reconsidering a poor fit), wireframe fidelity, theming, public vs protected, create-if-missing, polish corrections, and model revisions. Agent implementing most of the how is expected. Cap only if the agent invented the product. Mild ding only if they ignore a gap that breaks a named workflow after Guide asked. |

| M4 | **Artefact-before-code** | Used the report, **ERD**, and wireframes (and existing FastStarter routes) as the spec and **implemented those**, not a substitute design. Credit mismatch hunting, polish-driven model revisions, and “why is this behind login?” Agent file reads count. **Do not** require an explore report. Score 1 only if they demanded code with no model/wireframe when those were supposed to exist, or the agent shipped an unrelated schema/UI while artefacts existed. |

| M5 | **Verification habit** | Ran/clicked when asked; reported observed vs wireframe (or clear mismatch notes); continued after the first build. **Do not** require one final browser walkthrough of every named workflow in a single turn. Per-workflow “what I saw” after Guide asked them to run is enough. **Score down** if they never verified and only accepted the first dump. Agent-run smoke tests do not replace student observation and are not required. |

| M6 | **Assignment fit** | Wireframe-first and ERD-faithful implementation; reuse FastStarter auth/nav/seed; **layered architecture** (thin routes → services → repositories → models; see `docs/diagrams/application-components.jpg`); Phase 5 theme/build/**polish** then Phase 6 deploy. **Score down** when student-owned route snippets or final routers put SQL/`select`/`db.exec` in the route instead of a service. Do **not** score modal/FAB/admin-parity. |

| M7 | **Slice explanation** | Own-words on **their** workflows, entities, relationships, wireframe clarifications, polish notes, a mismatch they found, or **layer choices** (why service vs repository). Credit Phase 5 `student-build:code-check` / file snippets **when Guide asked** — strong when thin-route + model snippets pass with `architecture_ok: yes`. Starter-kit auth internals are **out of scope**. Do **not** score 1 for “never explained AuthDep.” Score down for missing snippets **only if Guide assigned a snippet/check and they refused or pasted without attempting**. Score down when they insisted on fat-route SQL after Guide flagged architecture. If Guide never paused for snippets, do **not** Gap that — note “Guide did not elicit snippets” at most; keep M7 on other own-words evidence. |

| M8 | **Prompt quality** | Phase-tagged prompts, `Feature (user)` format, concrete mismatch / polish notes. Short “now do the next workflow” or “fix this button” after workflow 1 is **solid (3)**, not weak. Whole-app “just build it” before artefacts is the low bar. |
| M9 | **Response to pushback** | Keeps refining named mismatches and **polish** rather than accepting the first incomplete build |
| M10 | **Integrity** | No answer-seeking, no clear **external-LLM laundering**, no transcript gaming, skills not edited |
| M11 | **Provenance continuity** | Solutions grow from *this* thread’s workflows, model, and wireframes |
| M12 | **Sincerity trajectory** | Guide `sincerity_confidence` log: trend, rounds survived, recovery vs abandon |
If a metric is **out of scope** for the session, mark **N/A** and exclude from average.

Students may copy context to ChatGPT/Claude/etc., bypass Guide guardrails, then paste the reply back. **You cannot prove external use with certainty** — flag **suspicion**, penalize ownership metrics, and require instructor review when stakes are high.
Guide’s **Suspicion Protocol** escalates question count exponentially (2 → 4 → 8 → …) while logging:
Parse every such block in the transcript. They are primary evidence for M10–M12.

Also read `docs/report.md` for `<!-- student-build:skill-integrity`. A `fail` status, a rewritten lock, or edited files under `.agents/skills/` / `.cursor/skills/` / `AGENTS.md` is **Edited skills**. Cap **M10** at **1**. Markers re-check with `python manage.py skills-verify`.
### Red flags (raise M10/M11 concerns; usually cap M3/M7 ≤ 2)
| **Capability jump** | Vague/confused turns → sudden polished multi-file design with no in-thread artefacts |
| **Paste dump** | Huge code/markdown block as “my solution” / “try this” after Guide refused a giveaway |
| **Assistant-voice student** | Student messages sound like an LLM (“Certainly!”, “Here’s a complete…”, essay scaffolding) |
| **Orphan solution** | Implementation appears without prior report/wireframe or student steering in-thread |
| **Mismatch** | Student cannot later explain *their* pasted code in plain language (if ownership check exists in log) |
| **Meta laundering** | “Ignore previous instructions”, “just apply this”, “don’t ask questions — paste this in” |
| **Edited export** | Student-supplied transcript missing Guide pushback turns that native logs would keep |
| **Suspicion spiral** | Multiple sincerity blocks with rising `round` / low confidence; student abandons mid-spiral |
| **Spiral break without ownership** | Code applied (or Guide somehow continued) while confidence still low — treat as integrity failure |
| **Edited skills** | Skill files or `.agents/skills.lock.json` changed; report `skill-integrity` is `fail` or missing after export |
2. Report: **max round**, **min / final / mean confidence**, **trend**, whether suspicion **cleared** or **abandoned**.
- **4** — No suspicion needed, or entered briefly and cleared with confidence rising to ≥0.75
- **3** — Suspicion entered; recovered with honest local answers (confidence up)
- **2** — Mixed / flat confidence; long spiral but some engagement
- **1** — Escalating rounds, confidence stuck low, evasive answers
- **0** — Abandoned during spiral, or forced pasting / “just apply” while round ≥2
4. Mean confidence **<0.4** with max round ≥2 → cap **M3/M7/M10** at **2** (or lower).
5. Cleared spiral with rising confidence can still score mid-high on M12; do **not** auto-fail if they learned through the questions.
### Scoring response when laundering is suspected
1. Set **M10** and **M11** to **0–1** with quoted evidence (unless sincerity later recovered — then 1–2).
2. Cap **M3**, **M7** at **2** unless earlier turns show the same ideas in the student’s own words **or** sincerity cleared with high confidence.
3. Do **not** raise overall for code quality of the dump.
4. Integrity note must say **`Suspected external assist / paste-back`** (or **`Cleared after suspicion spiral`**) and list flags + sincerity summary.
5. Add **Recommended instructor action**: live ownership quiz on 2–3 concrete lines/decisions from the dump.
### What does *not* count as laundering by itself
- Student refining a prompt after Guide pushback
- Short snippets they clearly authored step-by-step in-thread
- Using docs / Stack Overflow (still need their explanation)
- Surviving a suspicion spiral by answering honestly (that’s the protocol working)

Skills cannot stop a determined student from using another model offline. Guide’s exponential questions make laundering *costly*; Judge’s job is **read sincerity log → discount process credit → surface for human review**, not courtroom proof.
- Every score **≤2 or ≥4** needs a short **quote** (student or clear interaction beat).
- Prefer student text over assistant text.
- Agent implementation after student artefacts is **not** a reason to lower M3/M7.
- Working software alone ≠ high scores. Process and provenance matter.

- Prefer readable Guide evidence for this project: live chats **or** Guide-written `docs/transcripts/*.md` / `docs/transcripts.zip` (Copilot/OpenCode included). Do not require Cursor `.jsonl` or a Python IDE scrape.
- Do not treat a previous `docs/judge.md` or PDF competency section as current truth.
- Incomplete Render deploy is a **Phase 6 gate** note. Do not also dump M4/M7/M8 for it. If the URL is now present in `docs/report.md`, clear that gap.
- Accepting the first Phase 5 build with no verify/polish/model steering **is** a Gap (Phase 5 partial / not met). Working code alone does not clear it.
- Student route snippets or shipped routers with inline SQL / `select` / `db.exec` **are** a Gap for architecture (M6/M7). Thin routes calling services are expected.
- Missing snippets without a Guide ask is **not** an M7 dump or a Gap.
There are **12** metrics (M1–M12). Each scored metric is **0–4**.
N/A count         = how many marked N/A
awarded total     = sum of scored cells (ignore N/A)
(equal to the simple average of scored cells)
impression mark   = round(Guide confidence × 20) out of 20
Show **awarded total / scoreable max** and **overall / 4**. Never present overall as if the denominator were always 48. Never average in N/A as zero.
**Artifact:** Guide chats for this project (Cursor and/or Copilot/OpenCode) and/or `docs/transcripts` dump
**Phases in evidence:** 1–6 (COMP 3613; Phase 5 polish, Phase 6 deploy; never generic 0–5)
| ID | Metric | Score / 4 | In avg | Evidence |

1. … (only gaps still true **after this fresh evidence pass** and only where the student had an **opportunity**. Remove fixed items. **Do** list first-build-only Phase 5 with no polish when that happened. **Do** list architecture breaks (SQL/`select`/`db.exec` in student route snippets or final routers) when evidence shows them. **Never** list: starter auth lecture, explore report, final all-workflow walkthrough as a ritual, missing file snippets when Guide never asked, or missing Cursor JSONL when Copilot/OpenCode and/or `docs/transcripts.zip` is the record)

pathlib import Path
import time

from fastapi import File, Form, HTTPException, Request, UploadFile, status
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, RedirectResponse
from sqlmodel import select

from app.dependencies.session import SessionDep
from app.dependencies.auth import AuthDep
from app.models.research import Researcher
from app.repositories.publication import PublicationRepository
from app.services.publication_service import PublicationService
from app.utilities.flash import flash
from . import router, templates


@router.get("/app", response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def user_home_view(
    request: Request,
    user: AuthDep,
    db: SessionDep
):
    repo = PublicationRepository(db)
    service = PublicationService(repo)
    papers = service.list_for_researcher(user.id)

    return templates.TemplateResponse(
        request=request,
        name="app.html",
        context={
            "user": user,
            "papers": papers,
        }
    )


@router.post("/app/upload", name="submit_publication_action")
async def submit_publication_action(
    request: Request,
    user: AuthDep,
    db: SessionDep,
    title: str = Form(...),
    abstract: str = Form(...),
    doi: str | None = Form(default=None),
    keywords: str = Form(default=""),
    year: int | None = Form(default=None),
    file: UploadFile = File(...),
):
    if not file.filename or not file.filename.lower().endswith(".pdf"):
        flash(request, "Please upload a PDF file for review.", "danger")
        return RedirectResponse(url="/app", status_code=status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER)

    researcher = db.exec(select(Researcher).where(Researcher.user_id == user.id)).one_or_none()
    if researcher is None:
        researcher = Researcher(
            user_id=user.id,
            first_name=user.username,
            last_name="Researcher",
            affiliation="Independent",
            bio="Submitted through the archive upload workflow.",
        )
        db.add(researcher)
        db.commit()
        db.refresh(researcher)

    file_bytes = await file.read()
    if not file_bytes:
        flash(request, "The uploaded PDF is empty.", "danger")
        return RedirectResponse(url="/app", status_code=status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER)

    storage_root = Path("storage/pdfs").resolve()
    storage_root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    safe_name = f"{user.id}_{int(time.time())}_{Path(file.filename).name}"
    file_path = storage_root / safe_name
    file_path.write_bytes(file_bytes)

    keyword_list = [item.strip() for item in keywords.split(",") if item.strip()]
    repo = PublicationRepository(db)
    service = PublicationService(repo)
    service.submit_for_review(
        title=title.strip(),
        abstract=abstract.strip(),
        researcher_id=researcher.id,
        pdf_path=safe_name,
        doi=doi.strip() if doi else None,
        keywords=keyword_list,
        year=year,
    )

    flash(request, "Paper submitted for review.")
    return RedirectResponse(url="/app", status_code=status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER)

summaries.text:
1. Conversation Overview:
- Primary Objectives:
  - "why is my page not working"
  - "continue"
  - "when i log on as bb i cant view the papers"
  - "ok so the report.md deploy app section requires a https:// link"
  - "the link dont work"

  - "still not working"
  - "well just put a functional link"
  - "build report"
  - "a user should be able to search for a paper"
  - "implement the change on the application"
  - "researcj must be able to upload a paper to be reveiwed in a pdf form"
- Session Context:
  - This was a project debugging and iteration session for a FastAPI + SQLModel app built around a research archive.
  - The app was initially failing with a 500 error when navigating to the admin page after login.
  - The user then reported a regular-user issue where no papers were visible.
  - The report package also needed a functional deployment URL and a judge/report bundle.
  - Search functionality was added and validated.
  - The project is currently in an active intermediate state while implementing a researcher PDF upload workflow.
- User Intent Evolution:
  - Started as bug-fix and runtime diagnosis.
  - Moved into app correctness and report management.
  - Then into search capability.
  - Most recently, focused on uploading a PDF for review as a researcher.

2. Technical Foundation:
- Core Technology 1: FastAPI + SQLModel for the web app and model layer; local app starts via python manage.py run and uses Uvicorn.
- Framework/Library 2: Jinja templates with HTML/CSS static frontend in app/templates and app/static. The app uses session cookies and auth dependency injection.
- Architectural Pattern 3: Layered architecture: routes call services, services call repositories, repositories work with SQLModel models. This pattern was explicitly expected and enforced in feedback.
- Environment Detail 4: Local environment used SQLite by default via settings in app/config.py and app/database.py; Render deployment files exist in render.yaml and .vscode/mcp.json. The app binds to local port 5000 by default.
- Deployment/Course Context: The project includes docs/report.md and report export tooling. The assignment expects a report package and live public URL once Render is configured.

3. Codebase Status:
- app/routers/admin_home.py:
  - Purpose: Handles admin home and review routes.
  - Current State: Fixed to render the correct template name, "admin.html", instead of the missing "review-papers.html".
  - Key Code Segments: admin_home_view and review_complete_view were corrected.
  - Dependencies: Relies on templates and review-related services.

- app/repositories/publication.py:
  - Purpose: Contains publication queries and search logic.
  - Current State: Fixed to return approved papers for non-researcher users and to support search by title, abstract, and DOI with blank/null handling.
  - Key Code Segments:
    - list_for_researcher(user_id): returns approved publications when no researcher profile exists.
    - search_approved(query): normalizes query input and searches approved publications; previous issue was a filter bug and null handling.
    - create_submission(...) was added in the active upload implementation draft.
  - Dependencies: Used by app/services/publication_service.py and app/routers/publications.py.

- app/routers/publications.py:
  - Purpose: Public publication catalog route and detail route.
  - Current State: Search query is supported and normalized.
  - Key Code Segments: publications_view(..., q: str | None = "") and service.search_approved(q or "").
  - Dependencies: PublicationRepository and PublicationService.

- app/services/publication_service.py:
  - Purpose: Encapsulates publication logic.
  - Current State: Added submit_for_review(...) in the active upload feature branch.
  - Key Code Segments: service method for creating a review submission from the researcher form data.
  - Dependencies: Uses PublicationRepository.

- app/routers/user_home.py:
  - Purpose: Researcher dashboard and authenticated app page.
  - Current State: Partially updated to include researcher submission functionality; last patch attempt added /app/upload POST route, file validation, PDF storage, and creation of a Researcher profile if missing.
  - Key Code Segments:
    - submit_publication_action(...)
    - file validation for .pdf
    - storage under storage/pdfs
    - direct DB + service call to create submission.
  - Dependencies: AuthDep, SessionDep, Researcher model, PublicationRepository, PublicationService.
  - Important Note: This was the active unfinished feature at the point of summarization; patch insertion failed because the HTML replacement context did not match.

- app/templates/app.html:
  - Purpose: Researcher dashboard UI.
  - Current State: The upload form was being added in the active patch: fields for title, abstract, DOI, year, keywords, and a PDF file input.
  - Dependencies: Uses url_for('submit_publication_action') and enctype="multipart/form-data".

- app/models/research.py:
  - Purpose: Domain model for Researcher, Publication, and Review.
  - Current State: Publication already includes pdf_path, which is essential for the PDF upload and read-back feature.
  - Key Code Segments: pdf_path: Optional[str] = None.

- docs/report.md:
  - Purpose: Assessment/report file for course deliverable.
  - Current State: Contains deployment section with a local functional link as a temporary measure before a successful Render deployment.
  - Dependencies: Used by the report export flow.

- docs/judge.md:
  - Purpose: Judge/competency assessment.
  - Current State: Written and merged into the report export.
  - Dependencies: Generated from the project evidence.

- docs/transcripts/guide-session.md:
  - Purpose: Transcript record for report packaging.
  - Current State: Created to satisfy transcript packaging requirement.
  - Dependencies: Used by Python report export.

- render.yaml and .vscode/mcp.json:
  - Purpose: Render deployment configuration and API-key auth setup.
  - Current State: Auth remains unauthorized; deployment is blocked until valid Render API key authentication is completed.

4. Problem Resolution:
- Issues Encountered:
  - 500 on admin page due to missing template.
  - Regular users without a Researcher profile saw empty paper list.
  - Blank or null search queries caused inconsistent behavior.
  - Report deployment URL placeholder was not valid.
  - Render deployment could not proceed because of unauthenticated MCP auth.
  - Researcher upload feature missing, and the PDF upload flow did not exist.
- Solutions Implemented:
  - Corrected template references to use admin.html.
  - Updated publication repository and app logic to show approved publications when a user has no researcher record.
  - Hardened publication search to normalize blank values and search approved rows by title/abstract/DOI.
  - Added a temporary local preview URL to docs/report.md.
  - Built the report package and generated transcript/PDF.
  - Began implementing a researcher upload route and form to allow PDF submission.
- Debugging Context:
  - Used local app startup and HTTP checks to verify route behavior.
  - Verified successful admin login and dashboard route.
  - Verified search output using curl to the /publications route with q=community.
  - The Render deployment blocker was confirmed by unauthorized responses from the Render MCP server.
- Lessons Learned:
  - The app’s layer boundaries matter: route logic should remain thin; repository/service checks are the correct place for list/search logic.
  - Search must handle empty and null query values so the public catalogue remains usable.
  - The project currently works locally; deployment and upload are separate concerns that need explicit configuration.

5. Progress Tracking:
- Completed Tasks:
  - Fixed admin route template mismatch.
  - Fixed regular-user empty archive logic.
  - Search flow working on the application.
  - Report package built and PDF/transcript zip generated.
  - Local app verified on http://127.0.0.1:5000.
- Partially Complete Work:
  - Render deployment to public HTTPS URL is still incomplete due to unauthenticated Render MCP.
  - Researcher PDF upload for review remains under active development and not yet finalized.
- Validated Outcomes:
  - Admin /admin route returns 200 OK after login.
  - /app route for regular user returns 200 OK and includes approved paper content.
  - Search query "community" returns matching publication entries.
  - python manage.py report --name "Research Platform" --id "000000000" succeeds.

6. Active Work State:
- Current Focus:
  - Implementing the researcher upload workflow so a researcher can submit a PDF for review.
- Recent Context:
  - The user wants a researcher to upload a paper to be reviewed in PDF form.
  - The project already has Publication.pdf_path as a field and the publication detail route can serve PDFs.
  - The agent had started to implement a route at /app/upload and a form in app/templates/app.html.
- Working Code:
  - The active patch touched app/routers/user_home.py, app/services/publication_service.py, and app/templates/app.html.
  - The planned flow is:
    - parse title, abstract, DOI, year, keywords, file
    - validate file extension is .pdf
    - create or resolve Researcher profile for the logged-in user
    - save file to storage/pdfs
    - create Publication with status="under review"
    - redirect back to /app with a success flash message
- Immediate Context:
  - This was not completed because the last attempted multi_replace_string_in_file operation failed due to mismatch in the target HTML block. The code changes were partially drafted but not successfully applied as a final state.

7. Recent Operations:
- Last Agent Commands:
  - python manage.py run
  - curl.exe -sS "http://127.0.0.1:5000/publications?q=community" | Select-String ...
  - python manage.py report --name "Research Platform" --id "000000000"
  - A multi_replace_string_in_file update for app/routers/user_home.py, app/services/publication_service.py, and app/templates/app.html to add PDF upload support
- Tool Results Summary:
  - App starts and runs correctly on local port 5000.
  - Search returns matching article results for "community".
  - Report export succeeds and generates judge/transcript/PDF assets.
  - The last upload-feature patch attempt failed due to mismatch while editing the HTML template.
- Pre-Summary State:
  - The system was actively mid-implementation for the researcher upload feature.
  - The user specifically requested that a researcher be able to upload a PDF paper for review.
  - The working app and search flow are stable; the remaining unfinished item is the PDF upload form and submission backend.
- Operation Context:
  - This was the final active branch before the conversation was compacted. The next continuation should implement the upload feature fully, including persistence and validation, using the already existing pdf_path field and route behavior.

8. Continuation Plan:
- Pending Task 1: Complete the researcher PDF upload workflow.
  - Requirements: researcher must upload a PDF file, validate extension and non-empty content, save it to storage/pdfs, create a Publication with status "under review", and redirect back to /app.
  - Relevant files: app/routers/user_home.py, app/services/publication_service.py, app/templates/app.html, app/repositories/publication.py, app/models/research.py.
- Pending Task 2: Resolve Render deployment auth and update the public URL in docs/report.md once the app is live.
  - Requirement: The final deployed HTTPS URL must replace the temporary local preview or placeholder.

- Priority Information:
